newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Sept palm oil output seen little changed.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Sept palm oil output seen little changed.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil output in September is forecast to range between a fall of three percent to a rise of four percent in August production, plantation houses said on Monday.
"Production for September was down marginally because there was a rise rise in August. So the trees are taking a rest in September," an official at one plantation house said.

Malaysian private forecaster, Ivan Wong, who is expected to release his final September crop estimate later on Monday, forecast in his previous report that output in September will rise by four percent to 843,000 tonnes over August.
Wong said the absence of a pronounced seasonal peak also suggests that production will not drop sharply in the last three months of the year.
Official Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) September export/stock/output data is due on Tuesday.
Traders had estimated palm oil stocks at end-September at 910,000 to 920,000 780,000 tonnes compared with PORLA's 800,893 at end-August.
Exports in September were estimated at 640,000 to 655,000 tonnes against PORLA's 638,601 tonnes in August.
-- Tan Lee Lee, Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-2308911)
